The manatee is a large, fully aquatic, mostly herbivorous marine mammal, sometimes referred to as a sea cow.

https://imgoat.com/uploads/c8349cc726/44319.JPG

They measure up to 2.0 metres (6 ft) tall and weigh as much as 590 kilograms (1,300 lb)!

https://imgoat.com/uploads/c8349cc726/44304.JPG

Manatees use their flippers to "walk" along the bottom whilst they dig for beetus and gunetiks in the substrate.

https://imgoat.com/uploads/c8349cc726/44313.JPG

Manatees inhabit the shallow, marshy coastal areas and rivers of the North America, Western Europe, and parts of Latin America.

The main causes of death for manatees are human-related issues, such as heart disease and diabetes. Natural causes of death include vending machine accidents and choking on food.

https://imgoat.com/uploads/c8349cc726/44314.JPG

While humans are allowed to swim with manatees in one area of Florida, there have been numerous charges of people being harassed and disturbed by the manatees.
